findings.text: follow-on: the docstring says a foreign run reaches the running arm only "when ... its stream still moves inside the stall window", but the stale-stream case added by the same commit (:95-121) reaches that arm with a quiet stream, so the docstring misstates the reach condition and would mislead a reader about when the arm applies.

follow-on: the untouched comment says a foreign run reaches the arm "through the stream-in-motion reading", directly contradicting the comment the delta adds at :1062 ("reached whatever the stream's state") and the quiet case at :1068-1073; the delta left the stale sentence standing beside its own correction.

item_verdicts.diff: read both commits since the reviewed head a880b52 - f7ead92dc splits the foreign detail on the stream state, rewrites the test docstring without the plan-section citation and adds the stale-stream case, while 91938a188 rewrites one evidence-fragment sentence; three files, all inside scope.
item_verdicts.done_when: the section's done_when asks a temp-home classification of a foreign run with a moving stream to name the host and carry no "in-harness" with the in-harness wording unchanged; tests/test_a_run_on_another_node_is_described_as_such.py:71-92 asserts that and :95-121 adds the stale-stream case, and the manifest records the run and its result.
item_verdicts.goal: the delta's goal, stated by commit f7ead92dc, is to state the foreign run's real stream state in the running arm; reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py:1064 branches the foreign detail on `_newest_stream_in_motion(record, now_seconds=moment)`, saying "moving" inside the stall window and "has been quiet" otherwise, and both sentences leave the classification at "running".
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it records the head gate at f7ead92dc as 1543 passed against a 1539 base over 19/19 chunks EXIT=0, the negative control red at EXIT=1, and two retry failure ids absent from both final arms.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the manifest declares four write paths (reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py, tests/test_a_run_on_another_node_is_described_as_such.py, the evidence fragment and a figures dir); the delta's three changed paths all sit inside that set.

justifications.durability: tests/test_a_run_on_another_node_is_described_as_such.py:119 ("moving" not in row["detail"]) reddens if the foreign branch reverts to always claiming motion and is independent of the value the test passed in, though the recorded control trips the host assertion at :117 first and so does not isolate that line.
justifications.evidence: the manifest records the head arm at 1543 passed against a 1539 base (gate/head.*.log, gate/base.*.log, all EXIT=0), but the gate ran at f7ead92dc while the landed head is 91938a188, whose delta is one evidence-fragment sentence.
justifications.fit: the delta removed the plan-section citations the prior review flagged and follows the arm idiom at reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py:1049-1075.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py:1064-1073 states the stream's real state and :1058-1075 keeps every case reading "running", which is the delta's stated goal.
justifications.reuse: the branch reuses the existing `_newest_stream_in_motion` (reckon/crew/recovery_liveness.py:194) and `_record_is_known_foreign` (reckon/crew/recovery_liveness.py:948) rather than re-deriving either, and no other owner of a foreign-host stream-state wording exists.
justifications.scope_discipline: the three paths changed across a880b52..91938a188 are all inside the four write paths the manifest declares.
